\section*{Question 6}

Solutions to the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=x y^{3}\) also satisfy \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=y^{3}\left(1+3 x^{2} y^{2}\right)\). Let \(y=f(x)\) be a particular solution to the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=x y^{3}\) with \(f(1)=2\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(y=f(x)\) at \(x=1\).
\item[(b)] Use the tangent line equation from part (a) to approximate \(f(1.1)\). Given that \(f(x)>0\) for \(1<x<1.1\), is the approximation for \(f(1.1)\) greater than or less than \(f(1.1)\) ? Explain your reasoning.
\item[(c)] Find the particular solution \(y=f(x)\) with initial condition \(f(1)=2\).
\item[(a)] \(f^{\prime}(1)=\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(1,2)}=8\)
An equation of the tangent line is \(y=2+8(x-1)\).
\item[(b)] \(f(1.1) \approx 2.8\)
Since \(y=f(x)>0\) on the interval \(1 \leq x<1.1\),
\[
\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=y^{3}\left(1+3 x^{2} y^{2}\right)>0 \text { on this interval. }
\]
Therefore on the interval \(1<x<1.1\), the line tangent to the graph of \(y=f(x)\) at \(x=1\) lies below the curve and the approximation 2.8 is less than \(f(1.1)\).
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=x y^{3}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{1}{y^{3}} d y=\int x d x \\
& -\frac{1}{2 y^{2}}=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+C \\
& -\frac{1}{2 \cdot 2^{2}}=\frac{1^{2}}{2}+C \Rightarrow C=-\frac{5}{8} \\
& y^{2}=\frac{1}{\frac{5}{4}-x^{2}} \\
& f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5-4 x^{2}}}, \quad \frac{-\sqrt{5}}{2}<x<\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: f^{\prime}(1) \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : approximation } \\ 1 \text { : conclusion with explanation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(5:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { separation of variables } \\ 1: \text { antiderivatives } \\ 1: \text { constant of integration } \\ 1: \text { uses initial condition } \\ 1: \text { solves for } y\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}

Note: \(\max 2 / 5[1-1-0-0-0]\) if no constant of integration
Note: 0/5 if no separation of variables
